title: Smoothness detected by the conormal cofactor map of a curve
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $c\geq0$, $P=R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ for an ordered regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $B=P/I$, $C=I/I^2$, $V=\bigoplus_{j=0}^c B\,dx_j$ and $u:C\to V$, $u(\bar f_i)=\sum_j\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j}dx_j$. Differentials mean [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and exterior powers mean [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Write $E=[C\xrightarrow{u}V]$ in degrees $-1,0$ and $D(E)=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes_B\bigwedge^{c+1}V$, with $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B)$. Assume additionally that $B$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and every nonempty geometric fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is pure of dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $w:\Omega^1_{B/R}\to D(E)$ be the map with the displayed wedge formula of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ the following are equivalent: $w_{\mathfrak p}$ is an isomorphism; $w_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective; at least one $c\times c$ minor of $(\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j})$ is a unit of $B_{\mathfrak p}$; and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth at $\mathfrak p$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. More precisely, if $h\in P$ is a selected minor whose image avoids $\mathfrak p$, then, after ordering the selected variables first, the presentation
$$B_h=R[x_0,\ldots,x_c,z]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c,zh-1)$$
has invertible selected $(c+1)\times(c+1)$ Jacobian determinant $\bar h^2$, so it is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. On any smooth open subset the sequence $0\to C\xrightarrow{u}V\to\Omega^1_{B/R}\to0$ is exact and locally split, with last term a line. Under its relation-first determinant identification $D(E)\simeq\Omega^1_{B/R}$, the map $w$ is the identity. Equivalently, a conormal basis followed by a lift of a local differential generator is a basis of $V$, and its top wedge is the image of that generator under $w$. For $c=0$ the selected empty minor is $1$ and these statements apply to $B=R[x_0]$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), both smooth-locus implications; morphisms.tex Tag 02G1; algebra.tex Tags 00T6, 00T7, 00T8. Extracts old proof steps 5-6, including the explicit zh-1 presentation.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization] to identify $C=B^c$, $V=B^{c+1}$, $\Omega^1_{B/R}=\operatorname{coker}u$ and $D(E)=B\epsilon$, where $\epsilon=(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c)$. Expanding its displayed determinant formula along the last row gives $w(d\bar x_j)=(-1)^{c+j}\Delta_j\epsilon$, where $\Delta_j$ deletes column $j$ of the Jacobian (indices $0,\ldots,c$). The $d\bar x_j$ generate the cokernel, so the image of $w$ is exactly $(\Delta_0,\ldots,\Delta_c)\epsilon$. Over $B_{\mathfrak p}$ this image is the whole line precisely when one $\Delta_j$ is a unit: a finite sum of elements in the maximal ideal cannot be $1$. Thus surjectivity is equivalent to the minor condition; an isomorphism is necessarily surjective.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), wedge formula; Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), last paragraph; elementary cofactor expansion.

proof.text: On $B_h$, where $h$ is any selected maximal minor, permute the variables so its $c$ columns come first and write the matrix of $u$ as $\binom{M}{b}$, with $M$ square and $b$ one row. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], $M^{-1}=h^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(M)$. The map $v=(v_{\rm sel},v_{\rm last})\mapsto v_{\rm last}-bM^{-1}v_{\rm sel}$ has kernel $u(C_h)$: explicitly subtract $u(M^{-1}v_{\rm sel})$ to leave only the last coordinate. Also $M^{-1}$ followed by selected-coordinate projection is a left inverse of $u$. Therefore $V_h=u(C_h)\oplus B_h dx_{\rm last}$, the cokernel is free on $d\bar x_{\rm last}$, and the sequence is split exact. By the wedge formula of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization], $w$ sends this generator to the dual conormal wedge tensored with $u(\bar f_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(\bar f_c)\wedge dx_{\rm last}$. Its coefficient is the unit $h$, up to the variable-permutation sign. Hence $w_h$, and thus $w_{\mathfrak p}$ whenever $h\notin\mathfrak p$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), free-cokernel implication; algebra.tex Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse), adjugate calculation.

proof.text: The algebra $R[x_0,\ldots,x_c,z]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c,zh-1)$ is $B_h$: send $z$ to $h^{-1}$, with inverse furnished by the invertibility of $h$ and the quotient map. Order the selected variables first, then $z$, then the one remaining variable. The selected Jacobian, with relations indexing rows, is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}M&0\\ z(\partial h/\partial x_{\rm sel})&h\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and has determinant $\det(M)h=h^2$, a unit. Thus this is a standard smooth presentation by [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $D(h)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth. In particular a unit minor at $\mathfrak p$ proves smoothness there.

Conversely, suppose the morphism is smooth at $\mathfrak p$. Choose a principal neighbourhood $D(a)$ of $\mathfrak p$ contained in its smooth open neighbourhood. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $B_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-localization-conormal-split] to this original polynomial presentation: $u_a$ has a left inverse. In the conormal basis of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization] write these maps as matrices $A$ of size $(c+1)\times c$ and $L$ of size $c\times(c+1)$, with $LA=1_c$. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors], with $f=1$, says $1=1^c$ belongs to the ideal of maximal minors of $A$. Localize at $\mathfrak p$; if every minor were in its maximal ideal, their ideal could not contain $1$. Thus one minor is a unit at $\mathfrak p$. Together with steps 1--3 this proves all four equivalences.

source.place: Tag 07EZ (lemma-compare-standard), proof (e), split conormal sequence; algebra.tex Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse), part (2); morphisms.tex Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize).

proof.text: At every point of a smooth open subset, step 4 supplies a minor avoiding that point. The corresponding principal neighbourhoods, intersected with the given open, carry the explicit split sequence and line cokernel of step 2. Hence the original sequence on that smooth open is exact and locally split, with last term a line. On any such chart choose a generator $\omega$ of the cokernel and a lift $v$. The splitting shows that $u(\bar f_1),\ldots,u(\bar f_c),v$ is a basis: in split coordinates the last coordinate of $v$ is a unit. The relation-first determinant comparison sends $\omega$ to $(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(u(\bar f_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u(\bar f_c)\wedge v)$. Adding $u(t)$ to $v$ changes this wedge by zero; replacing the conormal basis multiplies its dual wedge and its image wedge by inverse determinants. Thus these comparisons agree on overlaps. They are exactly $w$ by [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization], so under the inverse comparison $D(E)\simeq\Omega^1_{B/R}$ the map is the identity, with sign $+1$ in relation-first order.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed relation-first formula and free-cokernel implication; elementary basis and lift checks.

proof.text: For $c=0$ one has $I=C=0$, $B=R[x_0]$ and $u=0$. The sole empty minor is $1$, the cokernel is $V=B\,dx_0$, and [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization] gives $w(dx_0)=dx_0$. The presentation of step 3 is $R[x_0,z]/(z-1)$ with selected derivative $1$. Thus all arguments include this case. If $B$ is the zero ring there are no primes and all assertions on open subsets concern the empty scheme.
